description: Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation between the National Cadet Corps of Sri Lanka and the National Cadet Corps of India
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-31 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The ongoing youth exchange programmes between the cadet corps of Sri Lanka and India contribute to the expansion of friendly relations between the two countries, and it is proposed to sign a Memorandum of Understanding between the two organizations to further strengthen the said cooperation. The said Agreement envisages the implementation of exchange programmes between the cadet corps members of the two countries for the purpose of planning and implementing joint specialized training and leadership programmes. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding for cooperation between the National Cadet Corps of Sri Lanka and the National Cadet Corps of India, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Donation of US Dollars One Million to the Government of Nepal
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-31 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The devastating flash flood occurred in the Rasuwa District in the Northern Nepal on 2026-08-26 has resulted in causing huge loss of human lives and extensive damages to properties. The severity of the disaster has placed a significant humanitarian burden on the Government and people of Nepal, and relief and recovery assistance is urgently required due to the continuing search for missing persons, the risk of further flooding, and the extensive damage to infrastructure. Taking into consideration the long-standing friendly relations between Sri Lanka and Nepal, based on deep cultural, religious and peopletopeople ties and Sri Lanka's experience in dealing with the devastating humanitarian and economic consequences of major natural disasters, the proposal made by the Hon. President to provide a donation of US$ 1 million as humanitarian assistance to the Government of Nepal, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Re-engineering the Vidatha Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-31 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Vidatha Programme was launched in 2005 to bridge the gap between national scientific capacity and rural economic development by making innovations generated through scientific knowledge and research accessible to rural micro, small and medium scale entrepreneurs. Vidatha Resource Centres have been established in 315 Divisional Secretariat Divisions as of now. The current Vidatha operating model, being structurally inflexible and relying on outdated skills and standardized programmes, has failed to adapt to the rapidly changing global market trends, the risks arising from climate change and modern technological advancements. Therefore, at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-11-10 approval has been granted to implement a Strategic Plan 2026-2030 for Vidatha Resources Centres, covering all 315 Vidatha Resource Centres located throughout the country. Under the said plan, each Vidatha Resource Center is expected to be operated under three specialized interconnected cells namely the Scientific Data Cell, the Incubation and Intellectual Property Cell and the Quality and Standards Cell. Accordingly, taking into consideration the proposal made by the Minister of Science and Technology, policy approval of the Cabinet was granted to reengineer Vidatha Resource Centers under the new institutional model.

description: Recruitment of Nursing Tutors on contract basis, for the Nursing Schools under the Ministry of Health and Mass Media
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-31 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - There are 17 Nursing Schools including the Post Basic College of Nursing under the Ministry of Health and Mass Media. The number of vacancies available in the post of Grade I/Supra Grade Nursing Officer (Education) in those colleges as at 2026-03-31 is 142 and since 24 officers are scheduled to be promoted to the Special Grade based on the vacancies available in the post of Special Grade Nursing Officer (Education) as at 2025-12-31, the total number of vacancies is scheduled to become 166. Also, there are 24 vacancies in the post of Special Grade Nursing Officer (Education). Although necessary steps are being taken to convert nursing schools into nursing faculties and upgrade the Diploma in Nursing to a Degree in Nursing, recruitment for the relevant training for the appointment to the post of Nursing Officer (Education) in Grade I/Supra Grade has not yet been done. Accordingly, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to recruit retired nursing tutors who served in government Nursing Schools and nursing tutors who have retired or legally discharged from the service from nursing schools belonging to the tri-forces, to the post of Nursing Officer (Education) in Grade I/Higher Grade, on contract basis, until the existing vacancies are formally filled.

description: Amendment to the Community Based Corrections Act, No.46 of 1999
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-31 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-04-07 to amend the Community Based Corrections Act, No.46 of 1999, by updating the relevant provisions to enable more effective enforcement of law against habitual offenders. Clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman pursuant to the said approval. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice and National Integration to publish the Community Based Corrections (Amendment) Bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter submit the same to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of the Quarantine and Prevention of Diseases Ordinance           No.3 of 1897
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-31 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Quarantine and Prevention of Diseases Ordinance No.3 of 1897 is the principal legislation in Sri Lanka governing the prevention of the spread of communicable diseases and the implementation of quarantine measures. However, it has been observed that the risk of transmission of communicable diseases across borders has also increased significantly due to the significant increase in international and domestic movement of persons, goods and services at present, and that frequent international travel and international trade are leading to the rapid spread of communicable diseases between countries. Accordingly, the Cabinet approval had been granted in the year 2016 to amend the Quarantine and Prevention of Diseases Ordinance No.3 of 1897, the said amendment Bill, but it has not yet been submitted to Parliament. Therefore, as per a proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media, the Cabinet approved to appoint a Review Committee to study the currently prepared Amendment Bill taking also into account the experiences gained during the recent pandemics and propose appropriate amendments to address current health challenges as well as future challenges.

description: Submission of the Orders issued under the Colombo Port City Economic Commission Act, to Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-31 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-03-30 to designate 68 business entities belonging to the sectors of Information Technology, Consultancy Services, Business Process Outsourcing, Logistics, Infrastructure, Hybrid/Combined Business Models and General Enterprises as Secondary Businesses of Strategic Importance under the provisions of the Colombo Port City Economic Commission Act No.11 of 2021. Accordingly, Orders have been published through the Gazette Extraordinary Notifications dated 2026-04-10 designating those 68 businesses as Secondary Businesses of Strategic Importance. The proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to submit the said Orders to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development of Road Facilities for the 'Tech City Project', Mahenawatta, Pitipana, Homagama
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-31 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The 'Tech City Project', Mahenawatta, Pitipana, Homagama has been initiated with the aim of making a high contribution to the country's economy based on innovation and knowledge-centered technology. The construction of the Western Bypass Road from Homagama, Walawwatta via Katuwana has been initiated in the year 2020 with the aim of providing direct access to the Tech City by avoiding traffic congestion in Homagama city. About 50 meters of the road section remains to be constructed to connect that road with the High Level Road. Further, it is planned to connect the Pitipana, Dampe road with the Kottawa-Talagala road through the interior of the Tech City via the access road from Sri Lanka Green University to the Sri Lanka Institute of Biotechnology. Approximately 650 meters of the said road remains to be constructed. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to complete the road section connecting the Western Bypass Road (Homagama, Walawwatta to Katuwana) to the High Level Road and the remaining construction work of the road from Sri Lanka Green University to Sri Lanka Institute of Biotechnology using local funds, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Continuation of the Humanitarian De-mining Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-31 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The primary objectives of the de-mining programme are to clear the landmines laid in Northern and Eastern Provinces during the conflict situation which prevailed in such Provinces, and release lands for re-settlement of families who were living in those areas to restore the normal livelihood of such families and development of necessary infrastructure facilities. Accordingly, in the year 2002, the activities of the Humanitarian De-mining Programme initiated by the United Nations Development Programme were carried out by local and foreign Non-Government Organizations and the Humanitarian De-mining Unit of the Sri Lanka Army. Under the said programme, 21.3 square kilometers of land area remain to be de-mined as at 2026-01-01. Currently, the international NGOs such as Mines Advisory Group and The Halo Trust, as well as local NGOs such as Delvon Assistance for Social Harmony and Skavita Humanitarian Assistance and Relief Project are engaged in de-mining activities as local and international agencies in collaboration with the Sri Lanka Army Humanitarian De-mining Unit. The National Mine Action Centre enters into Memoranda of Understanding with the demining institutions annually in carrying out demining activities. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply to sign 04 Memoranda of Understanding with the abovementioned institutions for the relevant work for the period from 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Signing of the Host Country Agreement for establishing BIMSTEC Technology Transfer Facility in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-31 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - At the Second Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) Heads of States Summit held in New Delhi, India in the year 2008, a decision has been taken to establish a BIMSTEC Technology Transfer Facility in Sri Lanka through a Host Country Agreement made with the host country with the aim of enhancing regional cooperation. The Cooperation Agreement for this purpose was signed by the relevant Member States at the Fifth BIMSTEC Summit held in Colombo on 2022-03-30. The main objective of this Technology Transfer Facility includes providing technology, capacity building and intellectual property management for micro, small and medium enterprises in BIMSTEC member countries. According to the relevant Cooperation Agreement, an Agreement should be entered into between the host country, Sri Lanka, and the BIMSTEC Secretariat to formalize the legal status, privileges and immunities of the Technology Transfer Facility. The relevant institutional approvals and legal clearance have been obtained for the Agreement that has been drafted for the same. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Science and Technology to sign the proposed Agreement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Bilateral Memorandum of Understanding on Immigration Control Cooperation between the Department of Immigration and Emigration of Sri Lanka and the National Immigration Administration of the People’s Republic of China
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-31 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Department of Immigration and Emigration of Sri Lanka and the National Immigration Administration of the People's Republic of China have reached a consensus for entering into a Memorandum of Understanding on Immigration Control Cooperation. The proposed Memorandum of Understanding is expected to achieve the objectives of facilitating discussions and visits conducted at the level of institutional heads and official representatives between the two countries, exchanging important official and intelligence information, facilitating visa, immigration and emigration matters affecting citizens engaged in business, investment, tourism, technological and scientific fields of both countries through an active and constructive approach, taking stringent measures against individuals involved in organized crimes such as human trafficking and smuggling and organizing workshops for the knowledge, skills and capacity development of officials. The clearance of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism and the Attorney General have been obtained for the proposed draft Agreement. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Public Security and Parliamentary Affairs to sign the said Memorandum of Understanding, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Treaty between the Republic of Korea and the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-31 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval was granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2023-12-11 to sign an Agreement between the Republic of Korea and the Government of Sri Lanka pertaining to granting mutual assistance in criminal matters. However, it has not been possible to sign the relevant Agreement between the two parties in accordance with the said approval. The said Agreement provides for mutual assistance by States to other States in matters such as handing over judicial documents and gathering evidence for use in criminal cases. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice and National Integration to sign the Agreement on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Signing of the Complementary Adjustment Agreement pertaining to the Technical Cooperation Agreement signed between the Government of Brazil and the Government of Sri Lanka for implementation of the 'Sugarcane Project in Sri Lanka'
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-31 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka entered into a Technical Cooperation Agreement with Brazil on 2008-09-16 for promoting bilateral cooperation in mutually beneficial sectors.  The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2026-05-25, granted approval to sign the Cooperation Agreement for implementation of a Project titled ‘Sugarcane Project in Sri Lanka’ between the Brazilian Cooperation Agency and the Federal University of São Carlos, the Ministry of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development of Sri Lanka and the Sugarcane Research Institute under the said Technical Cooperation Agreement. As per the Basic Agreement on Technical Cooperation signed between Sri Lanka and Brazil, it is required to implement the programmes and projects falling thereunder, through the Complementary Adjustment Agreements. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development to sign the Complementary Adjustment Agreement pertaining to the implementation of the 'Sugarcane Project in Sri Lanka' between Brazil and Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Drafting a Service Minute with regard to the establishment of a new Service category named ‘Specialist Medical and Specialist Dental Service’ in the Health Service of Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-01-12 to appoint an Officials' Committee to submit recommendations with regard to the establishment of a Service category for Medical Specialists and Dental Specialists. The said Committee has submitted its Report after conducting an extensive review. Taking into account the recommendations of the said Report, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to establish a service category named Specialist Medical and Specialist Dental Service and to appoint an Officials' Committee under the Chairmanship of the Secretary, Ministry of Health and Mass Media to draft the service minute pertaining to the said service category, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment to the Post of Commissioner General of Motor Traffic
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to appoint Air Vice Marshal (retired) Thushara Indunil Fernando to the currently vacant post of Commissioner General of Motor, on contract basis with immediate effect.

description: Civil Procedure Code (Amendment) Bill
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-01-20 to amend the relevant provision of the Civil Procedure Code, conferring powers on the Court to direct persons to give evidence through contemporaneous audio-visual linkage from a location at a remote point, upon a request made by a party or parties in a case pending before the Court, or a request made by its own motion, upon the agreement of parties through audio-visual linkage. Accordingly, clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the Civil Procedure Code (Amendment) Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman.  The Proposal made by the Minister of Justice and National Integration to publish the said Bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter present the same in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of Regulations on the Beneficial Ownership under the Companies Act, No.7 of 2007
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-07-21 to amend the Companies Act, No.7 of 2007 incorporating the legal requirements related to the registration of beneficial ownership of companies. Accordingly, the Companies (Amendment) Act, No.12 of 2025 has been passed by Parliament. The Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations, No.01 of 2026, made in terms of the provisions of the said Act, have been published through the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No.2480/48 and dated 2026-03-21. The proposal made by the Minister of Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Cooperative Development to submit the said Regulations, to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Preparation of the ‘Tourism for Heritage, Resilience, Inclusion and Value-driven Employment (THRIVE) - Nature’ Project for World Bank Financing
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Although Sri Lanka possesses immense potential for nature-based tourism, it has been identified that the growth rate of income has been relatively low despite the gradual increase in tourist arrivals. The World Bank has expressed its willingness to provide a grant of US$ 1 million for a period of 18 months under the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) for the arrangement of initial activities for a project called Tourism for Heritage Resilience Inclusion and Value-driven Employment (THRIVE) Nature for the improvement of habitats and development of infrastructure in nature-based tourism destinations. The proposed project will also support the further strengthening of programmes developed under the Ecosystem Conservation and Management Project implemented under the financial assistance of the World Bank. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to accept the said grant and to prepare the proposed project using the said funds, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the proposed Smart Meters with Time-of-Use Billing System by Electricity Distribution Lanka (Private) Limited
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2024-10-21 to obtain a loan of US$ 15 million through the Small Expenditure Financing facility of the Asian Development Bank to complementary projects that contribute to strengthening the country’s renewable energy efforts. At the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-09-03, approval has been granted to the use of US$ 2.5 million from the said loan to prepare the detailed design and tender documents for the Maha Oya Pumped Storage Hydropower Plant Development Project. The remaining US$ 12.5 million is proposed to be used to implement a project to install 300,000 Smart Meters with a Time-of-Use Billing System as part of Sri Lanka's Smart Grid Modernization initiative. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Energy to implement the said project by Electricity Distribution Lanka (Private) Limited within a period of 02 years was, approved by the Cabinet of Ministers.

description: Construction of the New Cardiology Unit Building of the District General Hospital, Trincomalee and the New Cardiology and Cardiothoracic Complex Building at the Teaching Hospital, Anuradhapura
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Health and Medical Service Improvement Project, with the aim of strengthening the services of diagnosis and treatment of cardiovascular diseases, was initiated in 2018 under the financial facilities of the Japan International Cooperation Agency. Under the said project, it is expected to improve the cardiac treatment facilities at the National Hospital, Kandy the Teaching Hospitals of Anuradhapura, Kurunegala and Badulla and the Trincomalee District General Hospital. Bids have been invited in accordance with the provisions of the Loan Agreement and the procurement guidelines of the Japan International Cooperation Agency to select contractors for the construction of the New Cardiology Unit Building of the District General Hospital, Trincomalee under Package 01 of the said project and for the construction of the New Cardiology and Cardiothoracic Complex Building at the Teaching Hospital, Anuradhapura   under Package 03. Five (5) bids have been received for Package 01 and six (6) bids for Package 03. Based on the recommendations submitted by the High Level Procurement Committee, following the evaluation of the said bids, the Cabinet approved proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to award the said contracts to M/s Maga Engineering (Pvt) Ltd as follows: PackageContract Value, Rs. description: The Project for the Rehabilitation of 14 Bridges Damaged by the Cyclone 'Ditwah'
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The People's Republic of China has agreed to provide a financial assistance for the implementation of a project to rehabilitate 14 bridges in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Northwestern, North Central and Eastern provinces that were damaged by the Cyclone 'Ditwah'. The said project has been planned to be implemented in two stages and 09 bridges will be rehabilitated under its first stage within a period of 18 months. The People's Republic of China is set to provide a grant of RMB 79 million for the relevant rehabilitation work. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to sign the Agreement between the Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development and the People's Republic of China for the implementation of the said Project and to declare the Project as a specific project of the Government of Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of Connectivity Roads for the Central Expressway Sections I, III and IV
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Central Expressway project is to be completed in four sections, and it has been proposed to develop connectivity roads to connect the said road with the existing road network in the Western, Central and North-Western provinces thereby improving efficient connectivity, accessibility and traffic flow between the road networks. Accordingly, it has been designed to develop 12 connecting roads with a length of 117.68 km for Section I of the Central Expressway, 14 connecting roads with a length of 83.98 km for Section III of the Central Expressway, and 09 connecting roads with a length of 81.36 km for Section IV of the Central Expressway. The provisional total cost estimate for the purpose is Rs.104.9 billion. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to implement the project to develop connectivity roads for Sections I, III and IV of the Central Expressway during the period 2026-2030, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Conduct of the World Health Organization Universal Health and Preparedness Review in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The World Health Organization (WHO) has initiated a new voluntary, country-led, and peer-reviewed mechanism to enhance the capacity of its member States to detect, prevent and respond to health emergencies. The said Review, called the ‘Universal Health and Preparedness Review’, will be conducted with the highest level of government commitment and support from political leadership, based on the concept of ‘whole-of-government’ and ‘whole-of-society’ approach. The Government of Sri Lanka has accepted the invitation extended to Sri Lanka by the Director General of the WHO to conduct the Review. The Review will go beyond previous national and international health security assessments of the Country and will strengthen intersectoral coordination, build optimal governance frameworks and ensure financial commitment. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to conduct the ‘Universal Health and Preparedness Review’ in Sri Lanka, by further reaffirming Sri Lanka's commitment to strengthening health security, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the 'Janaridhma' (SL-PULSE) Project to strengthen Citizen-Centred Governance and Frontline Public Service Delivery through the Regional Administrative System
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka’s Regional Administrative Structure consists of 25 District Secretariats and 341 Divisional Secretariats. This institutional system provides a range of essential public services including community development, social security, State land administration, disaster management, civil registration, pension related services and other citizen-centered administrative functions. At present, there is no national mechanism in place to systematically collect and evaluate citizens' feedback and experiences on accessibility to services and the quality and efficiency of those services. Therefore, considering the need to establish a mechanism for this purpose, the 'Janaridhma' (SL-PULSE) project has been planned to be implemented under the financial and technical assistance provided by the United Nations Development Programme to conduct Sri Lanka’s first citizen feedback survey on Public Services. The relevant survey is to be conducted island-wide, involving between 13,000 - 15,000 citizens, covering seven (07) key areas of citizen participation, citizen accountability, corruption reduction, public administration procedures, public services, environment and digitalization, under the levels of open public participation, community-based survey and random survey. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government to implement the 'Janaridhma' (SL-PULSE) project enabling to analyze the data obtained and implement the necessary reforms to increase the efficiency and transparency of the provision of relevant public services, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Strategic Framework for the Technical and Vocational Education & Training Sector 2026-2035 Skills Development System Transformation Programme - (Item No.08 and 09)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Technical and Vocational Education & Training (TVET) has been identified as a strategic pillar of the Government’s National Policy Framework to generate workforce equipped with skills to meet the national and international labour market demand. Although a large number of Government owned Technical and Vocational Education & Training institutes are currently operating, various challenging situations have emerged in the sector due to the mismatch between the content of training programmes and the labour market requirements. In order to overcome these challenges and create long-term development in the TVET sector, a Technical and Vocational Education Strategic Framework for the period of 2026-2035 has been prepared with the technical assistance of the Asian Development Bank as a key guideline. Further, a 'Skills Development System Transformation Programme' has been planned to be implemented in line with the said strategic framework. The said program aims to strengthen the G.C.E. A/L Vocational Education programmes, streamline the vocational education governing structure, improvement of quality and relevance of Technical and Vocational Education Programmes, expand equal access, develop training infrastructure, increase the industry sector participation, strengthen the digital transformation and introduce a sustainable financial mechanism for skills development and it is also expected to obtain the support of Sri Lanka's development partners for this. Accordingly, the proposals made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education to adopt the Strategic Framework for the Technical and Vocational Education & Training Sector as the national strategic guideline for the country's Technical and Vocational Education and Training Sector for the period 2026-2035 and to implement the 'Skills Development Systems Transformation Program' for the said strategic framework during the period 2027-2031.

description: Establishment of the National Business Facilitation Centre
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Local investment currently faces several major challenges, due to the circumstances such as the existence of fragmented approval processes spread across multiple disparate Government agencies, operation of institutions in isolated silos with minimal inter-agency communication, their issues on overlapping institutional mandates and administrative inertia. Among these, the existence of fragmented approval processes spread across multiple Government agencies with regard to a single investment project is a major challenge in initiating domestic investment. As a result, it has been identified that there are frequent delays in activities such as allocating lands for project development, obtaining environmental approvals and regulatory licenses, power grid connections, water supply and banking and financing facilities whereby investors are inconvenienced and get discouraged. Therefore, the need to establish a single coordinating body to guide entrepreneurs in the country in order to create an investment-friendly environment for starting a business has been identified. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President to establish a National Business Facilitation Center under the Presidential Secretariat to facilitate investors and to operate the said Centre with high authority to optimize policies in the industrial sector by removing existing administrative barriers to investment, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of the Bill titled ‘Protection of the State from Terrorism’ to Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - In view of the need to introduce a new law to cover the existing shortcomings of the Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act, No. 48 of 1979, a Technical Expert Committee has been appointed to prepare a preliminary draft in relation to the said matter. Based on the preliminary draft prepared by the said Technical Expert Committee, policy approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-08-10 to introduce a new Act titled 'Protection of the State from Terrorism'. Accordingly, the clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman. The proposal made by the Minister of Justice and National Integration to publish the said Bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter submit it to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of the Orders issued under the Colombo Port City Economic Commission Act, to Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-03-30 to designate Marina Hotel Holdings (Pvt) Ltd, as a Primary Business of Strategic Importance whereas at the meeting held on 2026-05-04 to designate Prime Melwa Port City (Pvt) Ltd, and Home Lands Port City (Pvt) Ltd, as Primary Businesses of Strategic Importance under the provisions of the Colombo Port City Economic Commission Act No.11 of 2021. description: Commencement of tourism activities at the Nildiya Pokuna located in the Ravana Ella Sanctuary under the supervision and regulation of the Department of Wildlife Conservation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Nildiya Pokuna, located within an internal cave complex of the Ravana Ella Sanctuary in the Karandagolla Grama Niladhari Division of the Ella Divisional Secretariat in the Badulla District, is a very rare natural water source. The place has become a very popular tourist destination among local and foreign tourists due to its unique geographical features. Since the Nildiya Pokuna is a rare natural resource that needs to be preserved, it has been identified as an essential task to properly monitor and regulate tourism activities at the place. A Technical Committee representing university professors and relevant government institutions has been appointed to obtain suggestions and recommendations for this purpose, and the Committee has submitted a study Report. Based on the suggestions and recommendations included in the said Report, the regulations prepared to regulate tourism activities have been examined and confirmed by the Legal Draftsman. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to publish the relevant regulations in the Gazette in accordance with the provisions of the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of the Orders published under the Companies Act, No.07 of 2007 and the Societies Ordinance, No.16 of 1891 (Chapter 123) to Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Provisions regarding the revision of fees charged by public institutions for the provision of services and the imposition of new fees have been introduced by the Public Finance Circular No.01/2020 and incidental circulars. Accordingly, institutions for which provisions relating to the determination, levying or revision of fees have been made by an Act passed by Parliament or any other law may revise the relevant fees in the manner prescribed by that Act/Law. Fees may be levied by orders in relation to the functions specified under section 527 to be read with section 477 of the Companies Act, No.07 of 2007, and fees may be levied by orders in relation to the functions specified under the relevant Act under section 19 to be read with section 20 of the Societies Ordinance No.16 of 1891, in consultation with the Minister in charge of Finance. The last revision of the service fees of the Department of the Registrar of Companies was made by the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No.2303/07 dated 2022-10-25. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Cooperative Development to the Companies (Fees) Orders and Societies (Fees) Orders published by the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No.2496/03 dated 202607-06, amending the said fees to suit the current circumstances, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the Foreign Exchange Act, No.12 of 2017, to recognize the unauthorized transfer of funds outside Sri Lanka as a criminal offence
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - If a person in Sri Lanka remits funds outside the country as an advance payment for the import of goods and subsequently fails to import the corresponding goods into Sri Lanka within a reasonable period of time, such a remittance can be considered as an unauthorized transfer of foreign exchange out of the country. Under the existing provisions of the Foreign Exchange Act, the only action that can be taken in respect of such unauthorized transfer of money is the imposition of a monetary penalty in Sri Lankan rupees equivalent to the value of the relevant remittance by the Central Bank of Sri Lanka. Since such unauthorized transfers of funds are not defined as a criminal offence under the Foreign Exchange Act, legal provisions for criminal prosecution are not available in the said Act. Therefore, it has been recognized that establishing unauthorized transfers of money out of Sri Lanka as a criminal offense under the Foreign Exchange Act will enable investigative agencies and law enforcement agencies to take effective action against such incidents under the relevant legal framework. Accordingly, approval of the Cabinet was granted in principle to the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to amend the Foreign Exchange Act, No.12 of 2017, to introduce specific provisions under the Foreign Exchange Act to introduce unauthorized transfers of money outside the country as criminal offences.

description: Awarding the contract for the completion of balance work of the New Hostel Block for the National Police Academy at Katana
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Department of Buildings, which is the procurement entity of the Project for the completion of balance work of the New Hostel Block for the National Police Academy at Katana, has invited bids under the National Competitive Bidding procedure to select a suitable contractor for the remaining works of the said building. Ten (10) bidders have submitted bids for the same. Based on the recommendations made by the High Level Procurement Committee, the proposal made by the Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply to award the contract for the remaining works of the new hostel building for the National Police Academy, to M/s Central Engineering Services (Pvt) Ltd., the substantially responsive lowest bidder, for a sum of Rs.614.98 million (VAT excluded), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Ensuring the structural stability of the laboratory buildings of the National Institute of Fundamental Studies affected by the Cyclone 'Ditwah'
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The National Institute of Fundamental Studies, established by the National Institute of Fundamental Studies Act, No.55 of 1981, is a premier nationallevel research institute conducting fundamental scientific research in Sri Lanka and making a significant contribution to human capital development. Due to the heavy rainfall accompanying the Cyclone 'Ditwah' that affected the island in November 2025, a landslide occurred in and around the premises of the National Institute of Fundamental Studies located in Hanthana, Kandy. As a result, the structural stability of the main laboratory building complex of the institute has been severely threatened, and there is also a serious risk to the safety of the lives and properties of the adjacent residents. After conducting the relevant geotechnical and structural assessments, the National Building Research Institute has recommended that reconstruction work, including the construction of a protective embankment, be implemented urgently to stabilize the damaged area. The cost for the said work is estimated as Rs.250 million. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Science and Technology to transfer the responsibility of managing the design, geotechnical evaluation and procurement process of the relevant project to the National Building Research Institute on a direct contract basis, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the projects for the promotion in the fields of Drama, Performing Arts and Literature
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- Although there are 09 sub panels representing 09 subject areas operate under the Arts Council of Sri Lanka, due to the lack of adequate funds, the activities of those sub panels are mostly limited to the national level and to the capital city. Also, the drama, performing arts and literature sectors are currently in a crisis due to the decline in audience, the decline in new productions, lack of theatres and the competition with the social media. Therefore, a provision of Rs.50 million has been allocated in the 2026 annual budget to implement appropriate projects with the objectives of revitalization in the field of drama, performing arts and literature at national level as well as regional level, empowering regional artists and bequeathing cultural heritage to future generations. The Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs to implement the projects as follows, using the said provisions:

Promoting the scopes represented by the 09 sub panels under the Arts Council of Sri Lanka at the regional level.


Conducting the State Drama Festival in a more diversified manner and implementing a programme to encourage new drama productions and performances.


Conducting multicultural art festivals based on multicultural centres.


Providing facilities to cinema clusters built around cultural centres.

description: Procurement of medicines through the United Nations Development Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Considering the procurement challenges in the uninterrupted supply of essential medicines and surgical consumables for the government health sector, discussions have been held between the Ministry of Health and Mass Media, the State Pharmaceuticals Corporation and the United Nations Development Programme to explore on the establishment of a reliable mechanism for the procurement of urgently needed medicines. Accordingly, a concept paper titled ‘Long-Term Partnership for the Procurement of Essential and Orphan Medicines’ has been submitted by the United Nations Development Programme and a framework for collaboration with the Government of Sri Lanka for the procurement and supply of critical pharmaceutical products has been proposed. The National Medicines Regulatory Authority will take measures to ensure that all medicines imported under the proposed partnership comply with the relevant regulatory and quality standards before being distributed in Sri Lanka. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to enter into a Financing Agreement with the United Nations Development Programme for the procurement and supply of essential pharmaceuticals and medical consumables, campaign and orphan medicines, so as to ensure the supply of essential medicines without any shortage, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Completion of the remaining construction works of Sethsiripaya                 Stage III
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - In order to meet the increasing demand for administrative office space within the Government and Semi-Government sectors, Sethsiripaya Stage III project has been initiated by the Urban Development Authority. At the initial stage, the estimated total capital expenditure of the project was Rs.16.7 billion. Approval of the Cabinet had been granted earlier to award the contracts for the pile foundation and superstructure of the project. Accordingly, the construction of the project commenced in 2021 and was completed up to the completion of 03 floors. However, the project was temporarily suspended with the mutual consent of both parties due to the difficulties faced on account of the economic instability in the country, shortage of raw materials, import restrictions and increase in prices in the construction sector. However, taking into consideration the office space requirements of the government and semigovernment institutions, the need to complete the construction work expeditiously has been identified. Accordingly, it has been proposed to implement the project as a joint financing development project to complete the remaining work of the project, and it is planned to complete the project by securing financial contributions in proportion to the amount of office space proposed to be allocated to the Ministry of Energy, the Department of Inland Revenue, the State Pharmaceuticals Corporation and the Urban Development Authority, which have been identified to be installed in the building. The total estimated cost of the project, including the cost incurred so far for the project, the cost to be spent on completing the remaining work of the project, other expenses and relevant taxes, has been calculated as Rs.38.48 billion. M/s Maga Engineering (Pvt) Ltd, the original contractor for the construction of the project building, has submitted a technical proposal including a financial proposal for the completion of the remaining works without affecting the original scope of the project and  followed by the evaluation of the said proposal by the Variation Review Committee, the contractor has agreed to complete the remaining works of the project for an amount of Rs.22.76 billion (excluding value of works completed, payments to be made, contingent funds, taxes and day works). Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to enter into a revised agreement with M/s Maga Engineering (Pvt) Ltd for an amount of Rs.25.58 billion (excluding contingent funds, taxes and day works) including the value of works completed and payments to be made, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of an expedited programme for the rehabilitation of minor irrigation systems damaged due to cyclone Ditwah
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Due to the cyclone Ditwah that hit Sri Lanka in November 2025, 1,599 small tanks, 1,686 anicuts and 4,042 irrigation canals have been damaged. Therefore, a problematic situation has arisen regarding the water supply and water management required for paddy cultivation. The Department of Agrarian Development is working to rehabilitate 883 damaged minor irrigation systems during the year 2026. In addition, there are about 5,935 small tanks, canals and anicuts that have been identified to be further rehabilitated. It has been observed that the damaged minor irrigation systems cannot be rehabilitated and completed expeditiously by utilizing the physical and human resources of the Department of Agrarian Development alone. As an alternative, it has been identified that the necessary technical consultancy can be obtained from the Mahaweli Consultancy Bureau, established as a subsidiary of the Mahaweli Authority of Sri Lanka, to complete the relevant work expeditiously. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Lands and Irrigation to allocate Rs.2,000 million in 2026 and the remaining amount in 2027 to the Department of Agrarian Development for the implementation of emergency projects, out of the estimated cost of Rs.12,170 million for the reconstruction of 5,935 minor irrigation systems damaged due to the cyclone Ditwah, and to obtain technical consultancy related to the reconstruction of those minor irrigation systems from the Mahaweli Consultancy Bureau, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing an allowance for students with special educational needs in low income families
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been proposed through the Budget for the year 2026 to provide a monthly allowance of Rs.5,000/- each for students with special educational needs. Applications have been invited from low-income students with special educational needs in low income families, studying in all schools in the Island to check their eligibility to provide this said allowance, and 5,530 applicants have qualified. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education to make provisions for the payment of the relevant monthly allowance to all such students, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Transfer of usable vehicles and machinery which belonged to the National Equipment and Machinery Organization, currently under the custody of the State Engineering Corporation to Provincial Councils, Pradeshiya Sabhas and Other Government Institutions
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A large fleet of construction vehicles and heavy machinery deployed for infrastructure and development activities across the Island, which were in the possession of the National Equipment and Machinery Organization, have been transferred to the State Engineering Corporation. The said assets are not currently being utilized by the State Engineering Corporation, and a significant amount of these vehicles are stored on a valuable plot of land located in the centre of Anuradhapura city. The North Central Provincial Council and several Local Authorities have made requests for the provision of said vehicles and machinery for use in implementing provincial development programmes for rural road rehabilitation, irrigation development and other infrastructure works. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply to transfer the vehicles and machinery currently in the custody of the State Engineering Corporation, which were then in the possession of the National Equipment and Machinery Organization, to the Provincial Councils, Pradeshiya Sabhas and other State Institutions, subject to payment of the Government valuation, based on the requirements of the said Institutions, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Signing of the Research Outsourcing Contract between the Korea Institute of Ceramic Engineering and Technology and the Industrial Technology Institute of Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A research concept proposal titled 'Development of Processing Technology for Quarts (Thirivana) and Silica Sand in Coastal Regions of Sri Lanka' submitted by a research team of the Industrial Technology Institute of Sri Lanka, was selected by the Korea Invention Promotion Association as an Intellectual Property (IP) Partnership Project in the year 2025. The said Project is scheduled to be implemented in two phases. The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2026-04-06, granted approval to sign the Memorandum of Understanding for its first phase, between the Korea Invention Promotion Association of the Republic of Korea and the Industrial Technology Institute of Sri Lanka. A Contract Agreement is to be entered into between the Korea Institute of Ceramic Engineering and Technology and the Industrial Technology Institute of Sri Lanka for the implementation of the second phase of the said project. The said Agreement will provide the legal basis for the Industrial Technology Institute of Sri Lanka to procure the necessary funds, materials, research equipment and technical support for the relevant research activities from the Republic of Korea with the assistance of the Korean Institute of Ceramic Engineering and Technology. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Science and Technology to sign the Research Outsourcing Contract between the Korea Institute of Ceramic Engineering and Technology and the Industrial Technology Institute of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka for the second phase of the project 'Development of Processing Technology for Quarts and Silica Sand in Coastal Regions of Sri Lanka', was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Agreement between Sri Lanka and Poland on Transfer of Sentenced Persons
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Transfer of Offenders Act, No.5 of 1995 has made provision for a citizen of another country convicted and sentenced to imprisonment by a Court in Sri Lanka to serve his sentence in the country of which he claims to be a citizen. Likewise, the said Act has also provided for a Sri Lankan citizen who is imprisoned in a specific country to be transferred back to Sri Lanka to serve his balance period of imprisonment. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice and National Integration to sign a Memorandum of Understanding on Transfer of Sentenced Persons, between the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Republic of Poland, enabling convicted persons to serve their imprisonment in their country and facilitating their rehabilitation, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Signing of a Memorandum of Understanding to expand the Cardiothoracic surgical services of the National Hospital of Sri Lanka by utilizing the facilities of the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Although the Teaching Hospital of the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University falling under the Ministry of Defence, possesses modern infrastructure, advanced medical equipment and adequate physical capacity, it has been observed that these resources are not being utilized to the maximum extent due to the limited number of specialist clinical staff. The Cardiothoracic Unit of the National Hospital of Sri Lanka, with its highly specialized human resources, advanced technology and state-of-the-art facilities, operates as the premier national centre for cardiothoracic surgery in Sri Lanka, but due to the increasing demand for surgery, there are currently long waiting lists. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to enter into a Tripartite Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Defence, the Ministry of Health and Mass Media and the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University to implement a programme to undertake surgeries and provide specialist care to patients on the waiting list for cardiothoracic surgeries at the National Hospital of Sri Lanka, utilizing the facilities available in the Cardiothoracic Unit of the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University Hospital, as an extension of the services of the National Hospital of Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of National Medicinal Drug Policy for Sri Lanka 20262030
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- The National Medicinal Drug Policy has been implemented to achieve the Government’s key health policy objective of providing safe, effective and  quality essential medicines at affordable prices to the entire population of Sri Lanka. Although preliminary work has been initiated during the period from 2020 to 2025 to update the National Medicinal Drug Policy for Sri Lanka, which was formulated in the year 2005, the said work has not been completed. Taking into account the experience gained in implementing the existing National Medicinal Drug Policy to date, prevailing health needs, changes in the global pharmaceutical market, challenges in the pharmaceutical supply chain and new requirements related to local pharmaceutical production, the need to introduce an updated National Medicinal Drug Policy for the period 20262030 has been identified. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to implement the National Medicinal Drug Policy 2026-2030 which has been formulated to achieve the following objectives, treating it as a matter of priority, was approved by the Cabinet.

Ensuring access to quality and safe medicines that meet international quality standards, relevant to the health needs of people at affordable prices in a sustainable and equitable manner.


Promoting the quality of care and preventing wastage through the use of scientifically sound, cost-effective pharmaceutical products by healthcare professionals and consumers.


Promoting the efficient local production of essential pharmaceutical products with assured efficacy, safety and quality.

description: Establishment of an Inter-Ministerial Standing Committee on Human Rights
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - As a member State of the United Nations, Sri Lanka is a State Party to 09 core Human Rights Treaties and 5 Optional Protocols. In addition to the said international Conventions, Sri Lanka also participates in the Universal Periodic Review (UPR), which provides Sri Lanka with the opportunity to voluntarily declare the steps taken at the national level to make progress on human rights. During Sri Lanka’s review under the 4th cycle of the UPR in 2023, Sri Lanka was given the opportunity to submit a voluntary mid-term report, outlining the progress made in implementing the recommendations received from other states, prior to the next UPR. Accordingly, the need to establish an effective multi-stakeholder national mechanism, including Ministries, Departments and Institutions of the Government, for the preparation of the said Report has been identified. As such, the joint proposal made by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism; and the Minister of Justice and National Integration to establish an Inter-Ministerial Standing Committee on Human Rights to serve as a stable national framework for an effective domestic process of follow-up and reporting on human rights activities in Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of an Education Council in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-17 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The need to establish an institutional mechanism for the standardization, registration/licensing, quality assurance and accreditation of all professional categories of general education such as teachers, teacher advisors, principals, teacher educators, education administrators, has been identified. A Committee chaired by Senior Professor O.G. Dayarathna has been appointed by the Secretary to the Ministry of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education to examine and make recommendations in this regard. The Report dated 2025-10-03 forwarded by the said Committee has been submitted to the Sub-Committee on the Establishment of the Education Council established under the Ministerial Consultative Committee on Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education of Parliament. Upon the approval received there, the Review Report prepared after consulting the public on the matters contained in the said Report has also been submitted to the said Sub-Committee. Accordingly, the Cabinet, taking into consideration the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education, granted approval to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a Bill to establish the Education Council in due coordination with the Institutions already vested with powers under the Constitution and other legal provisions with regard to matters falling under the purview of the proposed Education Council.

description: Appointment to the Post of Director General of the Department of National Botanical Gardens
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-10 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2024-12-30 to appoint Mrs. H.C.P. Jayaweera, Grade I Officer of the Sri Lanka Scientific Service, to act full time in the Post of Director General of the Department of National Botanical Gardens and she has accordingly continued to serve in the said post to date. The Public Service Commission has promoted her to the Special Grade of the Sri Lanka Scientific Service with effect from 2026-01-31. The proposal made by the Minister of Environment to appoint Mrs. H.C.P. Jayaweera to the Post of Director General of the Department of National Botanical Gardens on permanent basis to be effective from the said date, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Provision of immigration clearance facilities in the voluntary repatriation of persons, who left the country during the war period without using an approved port and a valid passport and have been granted asylum in India and have confirmed their Sri Lankan identity
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-10 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- Persons who left the country without using an authorized port of departure or possessing a valid passport for entry into India due to the instability that prevailed in the country during the war period, were subsequently displaced and registered as refugees with the Government of India and are now anticipating voluntary repatriation through the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). Advices of the Attorney General have been received regarding the provision of required immigration clearance facilities for repatriating them. While taking measures as per the instructions given by the Attorney General, Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Public Security and Parliamentary Affairs to make provisions for repatriating Sri Lankans who have left the country:

Obtaining a clearance report from the State Intelligence Service regarding persons who left the country before 2006-08-01 without using an authorized port of departure or possessing a valid passport and are displaced in India and have verified their identity as Sri Lankans through the Sri Lankan Overseas Missions in that country.


Verifying that they have not committed murder, treason and other offences specifically provided for or prescribed by law.


To issue temporary passports to the relevant persons and to allow them to enter the country through an approved port without taking any legal action in accordance with the Immigrants and Emigrants Act, No.20 of 1948.


To allow Sri Lankans who had illegally migrated to India within the period from 2006-08-01 to 2009-05-19, the date on which the war ended, without using an authorized port of departure or possessing a valid passport and have obtained a clearance report from the State Intelligence Service after verifying their identity, to enter the country through an approved port without being subject to any legal action under the Immigrants and Emigrants Act, No.20 of 1948, in accordance with the powers vested in the Controller General of Immigration and Emigration.


If there are persons who are liable for murder, treason and offenses for which special provisions are made or must be prescribed by law, they will be detained at the port and referred to the relevant institutions for further legal action.

description: Immigration Bill
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-10 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Despite the draft Bill prepared to introduce a new Bill to replace the Immigrants and Emigrants Act, No.20 of 1948 having been presented to Parliament, it has not been possible to proceed with the said Bill due to the dissolution of the Ninth Parliament on 2024-09-24. Thereafter, approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-08-18 to draft a new Bill, taking also into account the decision given by the Supreme Court in relation to the said Bill. Similarly, approval has also been given at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-12-10 to incorporate appropriate provisions in the said new Bill to designate the Secretary to the Ministry in charge of the subject of Immigration and Emigration as the Country Signing Certification Authority that implement the method of inserting biometric data into the chip of the epassport to be issued in the future. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Public Security and Parliamentary Affairs to publish the Immigration Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman, incorporating those provisions as well, in the Government Gazette and submit the same thereafter to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of the Fishermen’s Pension and Social Security Benefits Scheme Act, No.23 of 1990
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-10 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The need to amend the provisions and regulations of the Fishermen's Pension and Social Security Benefits Scheme Act, No.23 of 1990 to suit the timely needs and the fishing community has been identified. An Officials' Committee has been appointed by the Secretary to the Ministry of Fisheries, Aquatic and Ocean Resources to propose suitable amendments to be made to the said Act. The said Committee has submitted proposals to amend the Fishermen's Pension and Social Security Benefits Scheme in order to enhance the benefits received on contribution to the Fishermen's Pension and to ensure social security for fishermen in old age. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Fisheries, Aquatic and Ocean Resources to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a Bill to amend the said Fishermen's Pension and Social Security Benefits Scheme Act, No.23 of 1990, based on the said proposals, was approved by the Cabinet.
